newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EASIER IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EASIER IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted softer on Friday with the market expected to be flush during the day on maturing treasury bills, dealers said.

"Not much is happening at the moment. It's a bit quiet," said one dealer, adding however that the Reserve Bank was expected in the market with a treasury bill auction to mop up Z$1.3 billion expected from the maturities.

Dealers said Thursday's weekly tender had brought the treasury bill rate to 17.60 percent, down from last week's 17.72 percent, and discount houses were on Friday re-selling the paper in the market at 17.55 percent.

Bankers acceptance bills were indicated at 17.75 and 17.55 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 18.15 and 17.85 percent, while call money slid to 17 percent from Thursday's 17.75 to 18 percentage range.
NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90-days were at 18.40 percent (buying) from 18.75 percent and 18.15 percent (selling) from 18.35.
The Reserve Bank said the market closed on Thursday with a shortage of Z$109 million.
